request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
All the sheets in a tree now share one claim number sequence, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed** (server only; no database migration or front-end change was needed):
- `SheetService.nextClaimNumber` (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/sheet/SheetService.java:140`) finds the sheet's whole tree: the sheet itself, its parents going up, and its children going down. It locks every sheet in the tree, in a fixed order so two users can't block each other. It then gives the next number after the highest last-number held by any of those sheets, and records it as this sheet's last number.
- `SheetRepository` has two new queries: one for the highest last-number across a set of sheets, and one to set a sheet's last number. The old "add one to this sheet's counter" query is gone because nothing uses it any more.

**How it behaves:**
- **Every way a claim gets a number is covered.** Opening, splitting, a claim arriving from another sheet and renumbering all go through this one method.
- **Numbers already given stay as they are.** Each sheet still keeps its own record of its last number, and the shared sequence picks up from the highest of those.
- **Per-period numbering (e.g. `P1-1`) still counts per sheet**, as the request asked.
